checks.reason: Checked whether the strain source includes machine-compliance displacement and whether DIC measures local specimen deformation.
The two analysis methods are compared on the same tensile experiment, reducing specimen-to-specimen confounding.
Machine and DIC outputs are not independent replications; they are two measurements/analyses of shared specimens and loads.
The modulus and failure-strain claim is tied to the paired stress-strain curves and derived properties.
Checked which derived properties are sensitive or insensitive to the displacement measurement method.
The within-test comparison supports the bounded statement for the measured composites.
Agreement in tensile strength and disagreement in strain-derived properties arise from shared tests, not independent cohorts.
The claim distinguishes tensile strength from modulus/strain instead of collapsing all mechanical properties.
The measurement mechanism provides a concrete reason literature values can differ when displacement methods differ.
The study demonstrates the issue in one material/test setup rather than a survey of every literature system.
The supporting curves are shared-source evidence, so repeated derived properties do not create independent confirmation.
The literature-comparison warning is grounded in the demonstrated method sensitivity.
The exact bias magnitude is not generalized beyond the tested setup.
